Storozhnytsia Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpatska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews are believed to have arrived in Storozhnytsia in the first half of the 18th century, numbering just 4 in 1768 and growing to 325 (24 percent) by 1880. Following the March 1939 Hungarian occupation, dozens of young Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions and sent to the Eastern Front, where most perished; the following year, Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Nazi-occupied Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered, and the remaining community was deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. This cemetery existed at least from 1865, per its oldest found tombstone, and remained active until 1941.
